title: 3D World Simulator
subtitle: An action-conditioned world model that predicts in 3D. One predicted scene state gives 3D particles, spatially aligned tactile signals and consistent renderings from any viewpoint, interactively and over long horizons.
authors: Jimmy Wang1, Yifan Chou2, Kaifeng Zhang3, Yixuan Wang4, Binghao Huang3, Tao Yu5, Saleh Nabi5, Yunzhu Li3
teaser_caption: Teaser. Interactive use of the cloth model from the keyboard, the model's internal geometry and tactile predictions, four more tasks, a change of room and robot, policies evaluated and trained inside the model, and the same recipe on a larger set of deformable objects.
overview_p1:
We introduce 3D World Simulator, an action-conditioned, multimodal world model that supports long-horizon interactions at 50+ FPS on an RTX 5090.

Our approach involves a hybrid particle-voxel autoencoder and a 3D latent dynamics model that operates in a unified 3D representation space, providing a common interface to generate:
overview_p2: 3D World Simulator enables scalable data generation for policy training and evaluation using visuo-tactile and multi-view observations, including wrist-mounted and novel camera views. The 3D nature of our model allows for controllable variations in background and robot embodiments. When trained on large-scale data, 3D World Simulator generalizes to diverse objects, enabling downstream model-based planning.
demo_p:
Below, you can interact with 3D World Simulator across four robot manipulation tasks, either by using keyboard inputs or via dragging a gizmo to control the robot arms.

You may also view various features of our model, such as viewing the 3D geometry, novel and multi-view rendered RGB, tactile signals, and intermediate model outputs.
rollouts_p:
3D World Simulator supports diverse robot manipulation tasks, spanning deformable objects, articulated objects and in-hand manipulation.

Each video below showcases an open-loop rollout in which various model capabilities can be viewed, including novel view synthesis, multi-view consistent predictions, generated 3D geometry, and spatially aligned tactile signals directly represented as 3D particles.

Furthermore, we visualize intermediate representations of the model, such as its latent voxel representation, upsampled voxels, and raw model output before adding the 3D Gaussian static background and kinematic robot model.
backgrounds_h: Controllable variation in backgrounds and robot embodiments
backgrounds_p:
The 3D nature of our model enables greater controllability and editability through the incorporation of various 3D assets such as diverse backgrounds and robot embodiments.

While the base 3D World Simulator does not have any object-specific representations, it can be fine-tuned with segmentation labels to separate specific scene components, which can be replaced with other 3D Gaussian assets.

Since all scene components consist of 3D Gaussians, we can further use 3D Gaussian relighting methods to further add visual realism.
backgrounds_caption: Rooms and arms. Lab, gallery, warehouse, wood-panelled room and dining room, then the 2 × 2 comparison.
evaluation_p:
3D World Simulator enables scalable policy evaluation by rolling out policies purely within the learned world model. Our model shows high correlation between simulated and real-world policy success rates.

We evaluate policies that utilize visuo-tactile observations (Part Assembly), multi-view visual observations including wrist-mounted cameras (Cloth Folding), as well as novel views not seen during world model training (T Pushing). 

Our world model can simulate fine-grained failure cases such as in-hand sliding due to misalignment in Part Assembly, as well as missed grasps in Cloth Folding.
training_h: Scalable Data Generation for Policy Training
training_p:
3D World Simulator allows for scalable data generation for policy training purely within the world model.

We collect demonstrations via teleoperating the world model to serve as training data for policies that rely on visuo-tactile observations, multi-view observations, as well as novel views not seen during training. 

Policies trained with 100% 3D World Simulator data show comparable performance to those trained with 100% real world data.
training_caption: Real robot. Cloth, plug and Push-T policies trained on model rollouts, executed on the hardware.
objects_p:
To study 3D World Simulator's generalization capabilities, we train our model from scratch on the large-scale Deform360 dataset, featuring 198 daily-life objects, 1,980 interaction sequences, and over 215 hours of observations. 

Below, we show qualitative open-loop rollouts of our world model on a diverse set of objects from the Deform360 dataset.
planning_p: Since the model can imagine the result of an action sequence, we can plan with it: sample candidate sequences, roll each one out in the model, and execute the best. The objects here were not in the training data.
